a_resist_smoke_neutral.value: Resist Condition: Smoking vs. Neutral Cue

spans.text: Similarly, the left ACC, left PFC and OFC were activated in the entire group in the Resist Condition comparing the smoking-related cues to the neutral cues (Table 2 and Figure 2)

a_crave_gt_resist.value: Crave Condition versus Resist Condition (Smoking-Neutral Contrast) Utilizing Fixed Effects and Cluster Thresholding at p= .05

spans.text: However, employing a less stringent statistical analysis utilizing fixed effects, forcing the random effects variance to zero in FLAME (FMRIB’s Local Analysis of Mixed Effects: Beckmann et al., 2003; Woolrich, 2008; Woolrich et al., 2004) with a cluster threshold of p=.05, greater activation was seen in the Crave condition compared to the Resist condition in the left and right precuneus, left cuneus, and right middle cingulate gyrus (Table 3).
In contrast, comparing the resist condition to the crave condition activation was seen in the left frontal inferior cortex, left temporal superior pole, and left precentral gyrus (Figure 3).

a_distraction_crave.value: Crave and Resist Condition (Smoke-Neutral Contrast) in Distraction Strategy: Crave

spans.text: When the distinct strategies to resist craving were separated, the group that used distraction alone to resist craving, analysis with FLAME1+2 and clusters thresholded at p=.05, activation was seen in the left ACC, right OFC, bilateral precuneus, bilateral cuneus, left PCC, and left calcarine cortex during the Crave condition (Table 4).

task_description.value: Participants viewed blocks of smoking-related and neutral pictures alternating with rest, first allowing themselves to crave and then resisting the urge to smoke.

spans.text: Each epoch contained three, 24 second blocks: 1 block of smoking related images, 1 block of neutral images, and 1 block of rest with a static crosshair.
Stimuli were presented in a block design

spans.text: Stimuli were presented in a block design using standardized pictures of people smoking or engaged in neutral activities matched in frequency and gender
